A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Perturb-and-Revise and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Existing material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on 150 fashion-editing examples, Objaverse objects, and real scenes, including quantitative comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds qualitative comparisons and a preliminary 3D Gaussian splatting experiment.

M1.justification: Appendix D adds a preliminary 3D Gaussian splatting adaptation using mean and variance perturbation. The original NeRF parameter interpolation, adaptive perturbation selection, identity-preserving gradients, and timestep annealing remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 modestly extends tested scenarios with bear-to-polar-bear real-scene editing in Figure 2 and explicit separate-object placement in Figure 16 ('a tube of lipstick beside it'). The established fashion categories, Objaverse coverage, and other real-scene evaluations remain.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 2 adds an evaluated Instruct-GS2GS comparator alongside Instruct-NeRF2NeRF and Posterior Distillation. The comparator sets in the retained fashion, Objaverse, and other real-scene comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: The new 3DGS experiment compares perturbed and unperturbed Gaussian representations under stated identical conditions. Appendix E also narrows the reported resolution-milestone setting from fashion and general-object editing to fashion editing. This wording change does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds the 3DGS applicability experiment, a tuxedo example testing IPG preservation, and a spatial-composition failure case. It also revises the convergence snapshots. Existing quantitative perturbation and loss-weight ablations, and the intermediate real-scene analysis, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based repetitions, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Averaging across examples and metric backbones, and reporting optimization success percentages, remain unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds qualitative outcomes for the bear comparison, 3DGS perturbation, tuxedo refinement, and lipstick-placement failure. The convergence illustration replaces the 400-step snapshot with additional 700- and 900-step snapshots. Tables 1–4 and the quantitative perturbation curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: The main equations, particle-based variational-inference derivation in Appendix A, and interpolation-distribution proof in Appendix B are unchanged. The 3DGS discussion introduces no additional formal derivation or theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: adaptive parameter perturbation and identity-preserving refinement enable substantial appearance and geometry edits while preserving source identity. The state-of-the-art and training-free claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: V2 attributes PDS's restricted edits to its preservation term, explains layout-editing failures through pretrained-model compositionality limitations, and identifies adaptive densification and ill-defined Gaussian interpolation as obstacles to 3DGS adaptation. These extend the existing interpretations and limitations.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly clarifies that real-scene editing retains PDS's update rule and internal preservation term, and identifies LucidDreamer as the source for the Gaussian experiment. It removes v1's statement that supplementary code implemented in threestudio is included; actual external code availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds LucidDreamer and Instruct-GS2GS references and limited positioning around Gaussian representations. It removes the threestudio citation. The SDEdit analogy remains, although its numbered reference becomes an author-year mention.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract and several explanatory paragraphs, corrects the perturbation-study cross-reference, and adds affiliation and acknowledgment information. Computational efficiency and limitations move into dedicated appendix sections, while the main section structure remains.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 2 and 12, expands the convergence, IPG, and failure displays, and revises conceptual arrows and captions. Failure cases move to the appendix, and supplementary comparisons are redistributed across pages. Most existing comparison panels and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added comparator, preliminary 3DGS evidence, expanded preservation examples, and explicit composition failure modestly strengthen empirical support and clarify applicability. Core quantitative findings remain unchanged. Sparse details for the Gaussian experiment and removal of the supplementary-code statement limit the reproducibility gains, but the net improvement is supported.
